raw_response.printed_headline_estimate: Table 4, Model 3 (PDF p. 15 / p. 139, N = 1235, survey-design-adjusted heterogeneous choice ordinal logit with robust SEs): Formal ownership (formal-title dwelling ownership) OR = 1.84, p < 0.001 predicting higher reported household municipal-service coverage deficits (0 = no deficit, 1 = 1-2 service deficits, 2 = 3-4 service deficits across municipal water, sewage, electricity, and solid waste); bivariate association of formal ownership with no deficit is positive (p = 0.00, PDF p. 14 / p. 138), and supplementary Model 3 interaction formal home ownership X log head's years in neighbourhood OR = 1.93, p = 0.00 (Table 4 note a, PDF p. 15; 95% CI for predicted probability of no deficit: 0.01-0.99 vs. 0.14-0.98, Appendix A note b, PDF p. 24). Also in Table 4 Model 3 (N = 1235): Reported household community participation OR = 0.89, p < 0.01; Reported no. community organisations OR = 1.31, p < 0.01. In Table 3 Model 3 (PDF p. 11-12 / p. 135-136, N = 1235): Community or government action established municipal water service predicts formal-title ownership vs. non-ownership with OR = 2.15, p < 0.001 (predicted probability 95% CIs: 0.37-0.40 vs. 0.53-0.61, Appendix A, PDF p. 23).
raw_response.publication_year_note: Print issue date is January 2008 (The Journal of Development Studies, Vol. 44, No. 1, pp. 127-152, copyright 2008; PDF p. 1, 3); online publication date is 05 Jun 2008 (PDF p. 1); final version received October 2007 (PDF p. 3).
raw_response.rationale: Using a stratified probability survey of lower- to middle-income districts in San Salvador (sub-sample N = 1243; regression N = 1235), Tardanico (2008) estimates survey-design-adjusted heterogeneous choice ordinal logit regressions with robust standard errors (Table 4, PDF p. 15 / p. 139) testing a canonical Family A legal/tenure mechanism—formal-title dwelling ownership ('Household owns dwelling with formal title: 1 = yes, 0 = no')—on household municipal-service coverage deficits (0 = no deficit, 1 = 1-2 missing services, 2 = 3-4 missing services across municipal water [9% deficit], sewage [15% deficit], electricity [2% deficit], and solid waste [21% deficit]). Bivariately and with respondent controls only, formal ownership significantly predicts having no municipal service deficit (p = 0.00, PDF p. 14 / p. 138), but in the full model controlling for macro-structural assets (including an index containing indoor toilet) and log head's years in neighbourhood, formal ownership reverses sign to predict higher odds of service deficit (OR = 1.84, p < 0.001), explained by an interaction with log head's years in neighbourhood (OR = 1.93, p = 0.00; formal ownership reduces deficits only among newer neighbourhood residents/newer housing stock). Table 4 Model 3 also reports inferential estimates for household community participation (OR = 0.89, p < 0.01; Family B) and number of community organisations (OR = 1.31, p < 0.01), while social security coverage is positively associated with no deficit bivariately (p = 0.00) and univariately before becoming attenuated by macro controls (p. 138). Note for synthesisers: the municipal-service deficit outcome is a 4-utility composite combining municipal water and sewage with electricity and solid waste rather than a standalone water-only or sanitation-only indicator, and Model 3 adjusts for dwelling physical features (including inside toilet), which reverses the positive bivariate association between formal title and full service coverage.
